subject: Social Science
central_question: How do geography and monsoon systems create India’s varied climates, and how do those climates influence life, disasters and climate-change responses?
in_scope_units: Weather, Seasons and the Climate—short-term weather, recurring seasons, long-term climate and six ritus.
Types of Climates in India—alpine, temperate, subtropical, arid, tropical wet, semi-arid and tropical.
Factors Determining the Climate—latitude, altitude, proximity to sea, winds and topography.
Microclimates—valleys, forests and urban heat islands.
The Monsoons—seasonal winds, summer low pressure, winter reversal and southwest and northeast monsoons.
Climate and our Lives—traditional knowledge, festivals, agriculture, migration, prices and industry.
Climates and Disasters—cyclones, floods, glacial bursts, landslides and forest fires.
Climate Change—fossil fuels, greenhouse effect, warming, resilience, adaptation and mitigation.
Questions and activities 1–7—climate factors, cities, monsoons, festivals and disasters.
banned_topics: Advanced atmospheric circulation not in the chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Weather, season and climate mean the same thing.
known_pitfalls.correction: Weather is short-term, seasons recur yearly, and climate is a decades-long pattern.

known_pitfalls.claim: Coastal places have the greatest temperature extremes.
The northeast monsoon is entirely dry.
known_pitfalls.correction: Some winds cross the Bay of Bengal and bring rain to east and south India.

known_pitfalls.claim: Climate disasters are caused only by Nature.
known_pitfalls.correction: Human activities can increase risk and damage.

known_pitfalls.claim: The natural greenhouse effect is entirely harmful.
known_pitfalls.correction: It supports life; extra human-made gases cause harmful warming.

recommended_example_progression: Use Questions and activities Q1 to match climate factors and effects.
Use Q2 to compare weather and climate and explain coastal moderation.
Use Q3 to classify Leh, Chennai, Delhi, Panaji and Jaipur.
Use Q4 to draw summer and winter monsoon directions.
Use Q7 to analyse a climate disaster.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Questions and activities 1–7.
